title: Rethinking Temporal Knowledge Graph Representation Learning: From Entities to Evolutionary Event-Centric Clusters

problem.claim: Temporal knowledge graph representation learning commonly decomposes events into entities and relations and learns their representations in a low-dimensional vector space.

gap.claim: Existing research overlooks heterogeneous correlations among events, despite events being core constituents of temporal knowledge graphs.

contributions.claim: HEART models temporal knowledge graphs through an event-centric representation-learning approach.

A heterogeneous event graph construction module captures pairwise event correlations using co-entity and proximity edges, while an evolutionary clustering module captures continuous high-order correlations across timestamps.
Cross-temporal alignment preserves temporal smoothness of event clusters, and cluster-based self-supervised optimization trains their representations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on seven real-world datasets are reported to show state-of-the-art performance.
The authors report that HEART outperforms the runner-up by averages of 3.89% in MRR, 8.14% in Hits@1, 5.97% in Hits@3, and 6.92% in Hits@10.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prior temporal knowledge graph representation learning focuses on entity and relation representations.
Prior work does not model heterogeneous correlations among events.
HEART introduces event-centric graph construction, evolutionary clustering, temporal alignment, and self-supervised cluster optimization.
The authors report results on seven real-world datasets with improvements over the runner-up across four ranking metrics.

source_observation.claim: The approach represents events and their heterogeneous correlations through graph construction and evolutionary clustering.

interpretation.claim: When the core units of a temporal dataset interact in heterogeneous and evolving ways, modeling those units directly may expose structure missed by entity- or relation-level representations.

application.claim: Consider event-centric graph construction and time-aware clustering for temporal relational data where event correlations are substantively important.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether event-centric modeling is preferable for domains without heterogeneous event correlations or with different temporal dynamics.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the seven datasets, baselines, task setup, or statistical significance of the reported improvements.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational costs, ablations, or failure cases.
